sealed.statement: Separate the immutable replication TARGET from mutable replica IDENTITIES: desired replication factor comes only from a valid persisted partition policy row, creation initializes that policy from the schema declaration, and runtime replica identities never determine desired RF. A minted replace-replica-<hex> is a new identity, not a changed factor. Every behaviour-deciding reader resolves the target through one policy decoder.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Desired replication factor comes ONLY from a valid persisted partition policy row. Creation initializes that policy from the schema declaration, and the creation default tracks that declaration rather than restating it. Runtime replica identities never determine desired RF: a minted replace-replica-<hex> is a new identity, not a changed factor, and an identity count must never be written into the policy column.

Every behaviour-deciding reader of desired RF resolves it through the single policy decoder: readiness, quorum concentration, replica recovery, managed split, managed merge, existing-table reconciliation, learner voter promotion and the formation barrier. Diagnostic and display-only readers may remain outside it. No consumer may reintroduce a local interpretation after the decoder returns.

Neither INITIAL_REPLICA_IDS nor INITIAL_MESSAGE_GROUP_REPLICA_IDS is handed out by reference. PartitionService and MessageGroupService copy the peer list they are given, because raft reconciliation and raft lifecycle mutate it in place; a caller mutating its copy must not change what the next reader sees.

An absent or invalid policy row resolves undeclared and never silently borrows the creation default. The formation barrier is the one exception and it is deliberate: during formation the ledger row may not be hydrated and the creation default IS its declared policy, because seed registration creates that row with exactly that value. A zero target there is NOT fail-closed — it makes the cohort check false, barrierEngaged never latches, and BYPASSED_INSUFFICIENT_COHORT is a RELEASE state, so the barrier would disarm in the very window it polices.
The authority is a frozen projection carrying exactly replicationFactor and source; it mints no holders, no replica identities, no convergence and no readiness.
Proof is a deterministic node:test witness; every guard is mutation-verified against the final head with a harness that asserts the patch anchor is unique, and no cloud run is part of the proof.

claim: PLACEMENT-AUTHORITY EXCEPTION, transferred to S6. Measured on this head: system tables have no tables row, so TablePolicyService.getPolicyForPartition logs 'Table not found, using default policy' and returns replicaCount 3; move-planner.js:281 then computes its placement target as policy.targetReplicaCount || policy.replicaCount || NUM.THREE. That target, NOT partitions.replica_count, is the desired RF used to plan replica moves for critical system partitions. The non-interference test therefore FAILS its first clause: table_policies does determine initial critical-system-partition desired RF. Clauses two and three HOLD: neither formation convergence nor TRAFFIC_READY authorization consults that path. Semantic authority divergence is PROVEN; current formation causality is NOT proven, because persisted policy, table-policy fallback and planner target are all 3 today, so the divergence is numerically masked. Repair is deliberately deferred to S6 after causal measurement rather than changing placement behaviour before the S6a trace exists. S1.1's inventory is therefore 11 behaviour-changing desired-RF consumers on canonical persisted-policy semantics, plus 1 behaviour-changing placement-target consumer with known divergent authority whose repair is transferred; it is NOT 12/12.

Independent verifier rejected review-37557a9d40c999a47bee550d with seven findings against the final head, including a decoder bypass introduced by this round's own fix, three more behaviour-deciding readers, an identity-derived replica count gating admission, a cross-table creation default, a receipt whose prose contradicted the mechanism, and receipt coverage imbalance.

note: SUPERSEDED BY SPLIT, with its scope-pressure failure preserved rather than rewritten. The quest reached files=30 owners=9 and exhausted the blocked-scope override budget (3/3). The guard was right: verification proved this contains two independently provable layers, and each individual addition was justified while the cumulative candidate is objectively no longer one implementation slice. The invariant is NOT weakened — it is split into two truthful claims. A (replication-policy-authority-substrate, 15 files / 3 owners) owns the decoder, strict invalid/absent-row semantics, getInitialReplicaIds isolation, both service peer-list copies, the seed hand-offs that aliased mutable identities, per-table creation defaults, and the removal of identity-count writes into policy fields; A must NOT claim that every consumer uses that authority. B (behaviour-changing-consumer-convergence, 18 files / 5 owners) depends on A and owns the eleven routed consumers plus the inventory claim and the transferred move-planner exception. Both preflight under the guard limits (25 files / 6 owners), so no override and no ratchet change is needed.
